uncited: *   **Input:** Primary ray hit points ($P$), area light source geometry (defined by a set of samples or a parametric surface), and a user-defined number of shadow rays ($N$) per hit point.
*   **Ray Packet:** A structure containing $N$ rays sharing a common origin $P$.
Each ray $i$ ($0 \le i < N$) has a direction vector $\vec{d}_i$ pointing towards a specific sample $L_i$ on the area light source.
**Generate Shadow Ray Packets:** For each primary ray hit point $P$, generate $N$ shadow rays.
Each ray $i$ connects $P$ to a sample $L_i$ on the area light source.
**Traverse Shadow Rays:** Traverse the generated shadow rays in a manner identical to primary ray packets.
**Evaluate Occlusion:** For each ray $i$ in the packet, determine if it intersects any occluder in the scene before reaching $L_i$.
**Compute Shadow Factor:** The shadow factor for hit point $P$ is the ratio of unoccluded rays to the total number of rays $N$.
*   **Number of shadow rays ($N$):** Controls the quality of the soft shadow.
Higher $N$ yields smoother shadows but increases computational cost.
*   **Light Source Size:** The spatial extent of the area light source.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot T)$, where $N$ is the number of shadow rays per hit point and $T$ is the cost of traversing the scene for one ray.
The coherent traversal of packets may reduce $T$ due to cache efficiency.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ per hit point to store the ray packet.
The coherent traversal approach improves efficiency compared to independent shadow rays.
*   **Strengths:** Easy integration of global effects; smooth shadow transitions; interactive control over quality/performance trade-off.
*   **When to use:** When soft shadows from area lights are required and ray tracing is available.
*   **When not to use:** When real-time performance is critical and $N$ must be very low, or when hard shadows suffice.
This method is part of the broader field of ray tracing for volume rendering and light transport.
The approach leverages the inherent flexibility of ray tracing to handle complex lighting effects that are difficult to implement in rasterization systems.
